correctness.rationale: Theorem is a complete if-and-only-if case split: positive page edges enforce the opposite action when hubs agree, and compare a_i to b_i when hubs differ. The two hub stability inequalities yield exactly the interval H with weak endpoints and ensure the global complement factor two. Each equilibrium has cut weight A+B or tau+sum(max(a_i,b_i)); the maximum of the same two quantities is the global optimum and a Nash equilibrium by exact potential. The perturbation removes all opposite-hub best replies at any 0<epsilon<1/2 for even k and leaves exactly two optimum aligned profiles. Stirling gives the stated asymptotic along even k. A direct exact-rational verifier in the same complete package checked 2,605 weight settings and 318,360 profiles; these finite checks support but cannot replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The previously established equivalence between pure Nash equilibria and stable cuts and Lampis’s PARTITION reduction on symmetric K_{2,n} cover the subset-balance mechanism, not the full asymmetric positive-spine count, two-level welfare phase diagram and arbitrarily small perturbation collapse. Kun et al. already establish generic PoA bounds; no distinct exact book enumeration or perturbation law was located in the inspected primary material or targeted published-finding corpus matches. Originality is best knowledge subject to residual unindexed literature; no uniqueness claim from partition of subjects.
residual_risks: The already published symmetric K_{2,n} partition gadget is a genuine important overlap; only the joint positive-spine asymmetric count/welfare/perturbation theorem is assessed as new.
A general stable-cut theorem or an unpublished graph-specific table could encode the same statements without the book terminology; a bounded search cannot exclude this possibility.

The model concerns exact indifference; small perturbations can eliminate tied profiles, so the documented exponential change is a tie-sensitive Nash effect rather than a claim of robust strict equilibria.
Some publisher works and very recent unindexed sources may have escaped the search.

value.rationale: The triangular-book game is a concrete two-hub network in which weak Nash equilibrium multiplicity and price of anarchy can both be evaluated exactly for every positive heterogeneous weight vector, rather than merely demonstrating existence. The subset window identifies an intrinsic balance threshold for competing hubs, and the symmetric-to-asymmetric perturbation removes 2*binom(k,k/2) equilibria while changing PoA from 2k/(k+1/2) to 1. This is a quantitatively sharp boundary with exponential combinatorial scale and a welfare effect, not a routine restatement of the earlier partition-hardness mechanism or a single arbitrary finite example; narrow graph scope and tie sensitivity remain limitations.
